could_not_run_reason: No paper target exists for this dataset (targets.json is empty): the paper's only computed numbers concern 5DK3 and 6UMT, which are not in DVN/5BIH0P. What did run: the authors' xvg2csv.py (after a Python 2 to 3 print fix), the pre-registered internal checks I1-I3 and robustness checks R_a-R_c on the deposited per-frame MMPBSA data; the optional AmberTools 26 GB recompute (igb=5) from the deposited prmtops and 20-frame trajectory, plus R_c2 (igb=2). The production MD trajectory is not deposited, so no MD-derived quantity could be regenerated.

bugs.description: Legend detection `if l.startswith("@ s")` also matches the GROMACS '@ subtitle' line, and line 33 `' '.join(l.split()[3:])[1:-1]` then drops the first word and first character, so the CSV column header is wrong.
bugs.evidence: Deposited 2xwt-rs3-310k-200ns-rmsd.tab and 2xwt-rs3-400ns-310k-rmsd.tab (original-format downloads) have header 'Time (ps),fter lsq fit to Protein'; the .xvg has no '@ s0 legend' line, only '@ subtitle "Protein after lsq fit to Protein"'. Labels only; numeric values are unaffected (outputs/xvg2csv_check.json).

bugs.description: First column header is hard-coded as 'Time (ps)', but the RMSD .xvg files were produced with `gmx rms ... -tu ns`, so the deposited RMSD .tab files label nanosecond values as picoseconds.
bugs.evidence: xvg header 'xaxis label "Time (ns)"' and command '-tu ns'; last time value 400.0000305 in the 400 ns file and 200.0000153 in the 200 ns file, while the .tab header says 'Time (ps)' (outputs/xvg2csv_check.json). Labels only.

env_fixes: diffs/xvg2csv.py.diff: xvg2csv.py is Python 2 (print statements) and raises SyntaxError under Python 3.12; print statements converted to print() calls, output text unchanged. No python2 interpreter on the machine.

diffs/mmpbsa_gb_mdin_extdiel.diff: optional AmberTools GB recompute only (not the authors' code). AmberTools 26 MMPBSA.py rejects intdiel/extdiel in &gb and writes extdiel=80.0; removed so sander's default 78.5 applies, as in the authors' sander mdin.
class_reason: The paper reports no computed number for 2XWT (it appears only as a Table 1 metadata row), and the deposit lacks the production trajectories that its own analysis files were made from, so the materials cannot produce any reported paper number; nothing was blocked by compute or an uninstallable dependency, which is what E describes. The deposited code and MMPBSA intermediates that could be run were run (including a GB recompute with AmberTools) and are internally consistent, but that is not reproduction of a paper number.
confidence_reason: Class needed judgement (no paper target exists; C vs E is a definitional call), and A/B agreement is not yet known.
uncertainties: C vs E is a definitional judgement. I chose C because the obstacle is that the materials hold and can produce no number the paper reports (no 2XWT value in the paper; production trajectory not deposited), not a compute or dependency limit. An auditor reading E as "the paper-level analysis (re-running 200-400 ns MD) exceeds compute" could reasonably pick E; even then, a re-run would have no paper value to compare with.

The PROTOCOL class scheme has no "no reproducible target" category; any class assigned here describes the deposit, not the correctness of the paper's own 5DK3/6UMT numbers, which this audit did not examine.
I did not check whether the 2XWT production trajectory or the 5DK3/6UMT data exist in other ThermoPCD Dataverse datasets; the audit scope is this one dataset.

The deposited SD/SEM in FINAL_RESULTS_MMPBSA.dat are population (ddof=0) values; PREREG step 1 names ddof=1. Only the averages are pre-registered targets, so this does not change any check result; both SDs are in outputs/internal_checks.json.

R_a-R_c have no paper value to compare with, so same_direction_and_significance_as_paper is null; the pre-registered checks define no hypothesis test, so p_value is null (descriptive one-sample t p-values are in outputs/robustness.json).

The 400 ns RMSD series (2xwt-rs3-400ns-310k-rmsd.xvg) starts at about 4.48 nm at t=0, while the 200 ns series starts near 0; it was computed against md_1_30.tpr, which is twice the size of md_0_10.tpr. The cause cannot be checked without the trajectory; recorded descriptively, not as a bug (outputs/xvg2csv_check.json first_data_row).

The optional AmberTools GB recompute used AmberTools 26 on aarch64 (authors: Amber 21 sander, x86_64) and an mdin edit to restore extdiel=78.5 (diffs/README.md); it checks the deposited intermediates, not the paper.
The sandbox recycled once during the run (about 21:21 IST); the AmberTools install was restarted and all files on /workspace survived. No result file was affected.
